pattern.crimePattern: losing bidder kills the artisan who won a county tender
pattern.notes: Fictional businesses in the real Kamukunji jua kali sheds. County tender process shown in outline only.

ob.reportedBy: Fidel Okumu, metalworker, Moto Safi Jikos, Kamukunji
ob.text: Fidel Okumu, a metalworker, reports that his employer, Wanjiku Ngugi (41), maker of energy-saving cookstoves, was found dead in her shed at the Kamukunji jua kali sheds at 15:12, when he returned from a delivery.

people.name: Wanjiku Ngugi
people.bio: Makes energy-saving charcoal jikos. Last month she won a county tender to supply 500 stoves to schools.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, early 40s, welding goggles pushed up on a headscarf, soot on her cheek, a leather apron over overalls, proud and capable, ID-photo framing

people.name: Benson Okiror
people.occupation: Rival jiko maker, two sheds down
people.bio: Thirty years at Kamukunji. Lost the county tender to Wanjiku and lodged an appeal at City Hall.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 50s, thick forearms, a sleeveless vest over a work shirt, a hammer hanging from a loop on his belt, hard set jaw, ID-photo framing

people.name: Gitau Mwaura
people.bio: Borrowed against her tender advance without asking her.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 40s, office shirt and tie loosened, a small girl's pink school bag over one shoulder, ashamed, ID-photo framing

people.name: Fidel Okumu
people.bio: Has worked for Wanjiku for three years. She docked his pay last week for a spoiled batch.

image.brief: Kenyan young man, mid 20s, sweat-stained T-shirt, metal filings on his forearms, a delivery note book in his back pocket, shocked, ID-photo framing

people.name: Simeon Wachira
people.occupation: Old fundi in the next shed
people.bio: Forty years at the anvil. Can tell whose hammer made a dent by looking at it.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 30s, a pressed shirt and tie, a staff lanyard with the card turned round, cautious and polite, ID-photo framing

people.name: Samwel Marwa

locations.name: Moto Safi Jikos, Kamukunji jua kali sheds
locations.description: Rows of open tin-roofed sheds and the noise of a hundred hammers. Wanjiku's shed: an anvil with a half-finished stove on it, sheet-metal offcuts, a wall of tools on hooks, a tender board nailed to a post.

hotspots.label: Tender board

hotspots.label: Exercise book on the bench
hotspots.text: Her accounts book. The last page is underlined twice.

hotspots.label: Next shed

facts.text: Fidel Okumu found his employer Wanjiku Ngugi dead in her shed at 15:12, when he came back from a delivery.
Wanjiku was struck with a hammer. There is no hammer at the scene.
Her own hammer hangs on its hook on the wall, clean.
The half-finished stove on her anvil has fresh dents, each with a small X-shaped mark in the middle.
Tender board: 500 jikos for schools awarded to Moto Safi Jikos. Pinned under it: 'APPEAL LODGED — B. Okiror. Hearing Monday, City Hall.'
Her accounts book: 'Tender advance KSh 200,000 — WITHDRAWN by G. Mwaura without my signature!!'
Job card: '13:50 — 20 stoves to Kariobangi school — Fidel, handcart.' '14:00 — sample stove collected by school driver S. Marwa.'
Simeon: "Every hammer wears its own face. An X like that is a chipped face. Okiror chipped his on a rivet last year and never ground it down."
Simeon: at about 14:20 he saw Benson walk into Wanjiku's shed with his hammer in his hand, "like a man going to fix something". Then shouting.
Simeon: Fidel left with the handcart of stoves at 13:50 and came back at 15:10.
Simeon was at his own anvil all afternoon with his two apprentices.
Samwel Marwa: he collected a sample stove from Wanjiku at 14:00. She was fine, joking about the 500.
Letter from the county procurement office, dated today: Benson Okiror's appeal against the tender award is dismissed. Clerk: E. Koech.
City Hall visitor register: 'B. Okiror — in 12:10 — out 13:40.'
Edwin Koech was at his desk at City Hall all afternoon; he signed the register himself.
Benson's hammer, locked in his toolbox: an X-shaped chip in the face, wiped, with fresh metal shavings packed in the chip.
Clinic card for their daughter, Umoja Health Centre: in 13:30, out 15:30, with her father, G. Mwaura.
Fidel's delivery note: 20 stoves to a school in Kariobangi, signed by the bursar at 14:35.
Benson: "I was at City Hall all afternoon about my appeal. I didn't come back to Kamukunji until four."
Benson: "She won with bribes. Everyone knows."
Benson admits he left City Hall at 13:40 and came back to the sheds. He says he went into her shed to show her where her stoves were badly made, and she was alive when he left.
Gitau: "I was at the clinic with our daughter all afternoon."
Gitau admits he took KSh 200,000 of her tender advance to pay a debt, without asking her. "I was going to put it back."
Fidel: "I was delivering stoves to the school."
Fidel: "Mama never left dents like that. She would have beaten them out before lunch."

interrogations.intro: Benson wipes his hands on a rag that doesn't need it. "Wanjiku? God rest her. We competed. That is business."

topics.reply: Bad work. Soft metal, too thin. I have been saying it to the county for a month.
Call the clerk at City Hall, Koech. He will tell you I was there.
Dismissed. They didn't even read it.

interrogations.intro: Gitau holds his daughter's pink school bag in both hands. "I was at the clinic with our girl. They called me there."

topics.reply: I took it. Two hundred thousand. A debt from before, men were coming to the house. I was going to put it back before she noticed.

interrogations.intro: Fidel stands outside the shed and won't look in. "I took the stoves. I came back. That is all I know."

topics.reply: Mama never left dents like that. Never. She would have beaten them out before lunch.
She docked me for a spoiled batch. I was angry one day. Then she bought me lunch.

interrogations.intro: Simeon runs his thumb over the dents on the stove, one by one. "This is not her hammer. I know her hammer."

topics.reply: Every hammer wears its own face. An X like that is a chip. Okiror's has an X. He chipped it on a rivet last year and was too proud to grind it.
The school driver took a sample at two. Call him; the number is on her job card.

contradictions.reaction: I left early, yes. Twenty to two. They threw out my appeal in ten minutes. I came back and went to tell her what I thought of her stoves. Yes, I went in. She was alive when I walked out.

prosecutor.pass: He lied about City Hall, he walked in with a hammer, and his hammer signed every dent. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. A husband who stole from her is a thief. Was he in that shed?
No. Read the dents. Every hammer in that market signs its work.

proof.concludes: Benson said he was at City Hall until four, but the register signs him out at 13:40. Pressed, he admits he came back and went into her shed.
Wanjiku was alive at 14:00. At 14:20 Benson walked into her shed with his hammer in his hand.
The dents on her stove carry the X of a chipped hammer face, and Benson's hammer has exactly that chip, with fresh shavings in it. Benson Okiror killed Wanjiku.

eliminations.why: Gitau was at Umoja Health Centre with their daughter from 13:30 to 15:30.
Fidel left with the handcart at 13:50, had the delivery signed in Kariobangi at 14:35, and came back at 15:10.
Simeon was at his own anvil all afternoon with his two apprentices.
Edwin was at his desk at City Hall all afternoon.

reconstruction.text: Last month. The county awards 500 school jikos to Wanjiku. Benson, thirty years at Kamukunji, lodges an appeal.
Monday, 13:30. City Hall throws the appeal out in ten minutes. He signs out at 13:40 and goes back to the sheds.
14:20. He walks into her shed with his hammer, "to show her where her stoves are badly made". Simeon, at the next anvil, sees him go in.
They shout. He strikes her. Then he hammers dents all over her half-finished stove, to make it look like a fight over work.
He locks his hammer in his toolbox. Every dent he made carries the X of the chip he never ground out.

tier1.line: Look at the middle of every dent. Then ask the oldest man in the sheds what he sees.

tier2.line: An X in every dent, and an old fundi who knows whose hammer has an X. You have grounds for the toolbox.

glossary.def: The informal artisan sector; literally "fierce sun", because the work is done in the open.
A tender: a public contract put out to bid.
Mother; also a respectful way to address or name a woman.

ui.beatNotes: The comparison view: two pieces of evidence (the dented stove and the hammer face) are laid side by side under a magnifier and turned to line up. A match snaps with a click. Used for tool marks, handwriting, stamps and footprints from here on.
